mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate signals accommodative monetary policy that reduces equity discount rates, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days without threshold requirements.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in >55% of periods with declining FEDFUNDS, or Rank IC < 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate exceeding 5.5% for two consecutive months signals labor market deterioration that reduces consumer spending confidence, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in >55% of periods with UNRATE > 5.5% for two months, or Rank IC < 0.02 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates robust consumer demand that elevates corporate earnings expectations, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in >55% of periods with rising HOUST and RSAFS, or Rank IC < 0.02 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Monetary tightening regime (FEDFUNDS > 4.5%) increases borrowing costs and reduces equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in >55% of periods with FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, or Rank IC < 0.02 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Quarterly GDP growth above 1.5% (GDPC1) signals expanding economic activity that boosts corporate profits, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days without thresholds.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in >55% of quarters with GDPC1 growth >1.5%, or Rank IC < 0.02 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production falling below 95 for two consecutive months signals manufacturing contraction that reduces corporate revenue expectations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in >55% of periods with INDPRO < 95 for two months, or Rank IC < 0.02 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent employment growth (PAYEMS) and unemployment decline (UNRATE) indicate labor market strength that increases consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in >55% of periods with rising PAYEMS and falling UNRATE, or Rank IC < 0.02 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Housing market boom (HOUST > 1100) signals elevated consumer confidence and disposable income, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days in this specific regime.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in >55% of periods with HOUST > 1100, or Rank IC < 0.02 over any 2-year window.
